grh_ea6a7bfc72a26f1aa2da.title: Story Of Harry Monroe A Scarf
paragraphs: Judy's married friend Isabel Taylor feels trapped by quiet domestic life and secretly goes out with former beau Harry Monroe while her husband Kenneth is away. Harry has been drinking and drives his car into a ditch; frightened that he may be badly hurt, Isabel runs home and leaves behind a scarf she had borrowed from Judy. When the scarf is found in Harry's car, local gossip Edna assumes Judy was the woman with him. Judy claims the scarf rather than expose Isabel, even though the story could damage Judy's own reputation. Dr. Christian eventually gets the truth from her and turns the scarf into the solution. During a talk to Edna's club on first aid, he uses it to demonstrate an emergency sling and casually says that he himself left the scarf in Harry's car while treating Harry after the accident. The explanation protects Isabel, clears Judy without betraying her friend, and leaves Edna with no scandal to spread.

grh_ea0894953cebf3562c2e.title: Black Magic
paragraphs: Dr. Christian recalls a case in which Molly became ill after an asparagus dinner and developed a startling black discoloration of her mouth and tongue. Her doctor blamed poisoned food, and attorney Jernigan prepared a damage suit against grocer George Pullos for selling bad asparagus. Asked to investigate for the defense, Christian learns that Molly has also been taking a prescribed beef, iron and wine tonic. He realizes the dramatic black coloring is not proof of food poisoning at all: compounds in the asparagus react with the iron in the medicine and form a dark, ink-like color. Christian demonstrates the effect on himself in court by eating asparagus and taking the same tonic. The supposedly mysterious 'black magic' is exposed as an ordinary chemical reaction, the case against Pullos collapses, and Jernigan disappears rather than continue the failed claim.

grh_eae26ccf6a9b004925ff.title: Evelyn Briggs
paragraphs: On a fishing vacation near the Canadian border, Kildare diagnoses fellow guest Evelyn Briggs with diphtheria and insists that the Holiday Guest House be quarantined. Innkeeper Charlie Converse refuses, then hides Evelyn and makes her room appear unused because he is secretly sheltering Chuck Rivers, an FBI fugitive who has paid him to stay hidden until he can cross into Canada. Rivers and Converse force Kildare and Gillespie onto a train, but Kildare returns while Gillespie seeks county authorities; faced with an impending search, Converse admits that Evelyn is concealed in the attic. The doctors reach and treat the dangerously ill girl, while Kildare stalls Rivers long enough for the law to close in, turning their planned vacation into an emergency fight to stop both a criminal and a possible epidemic.

grh_ea0ebb87ffc81c6a35db.title: Tomorrow Will Sing
paragraphs: A dramatization of Elliott Arnold's Tomorrow Will Sing follows Italian-American airman Eddie Amato as he helps villagers near his wartime base understand American democratic ideas. The farmers come to trust Eddie while confronting old fascist influence and unfair economic practices, but he is later court-martialed after being accused of robbing local peasants. Testimony finally exposes a former Blackshirt's son as the real thief, clearing Eddie; the story closes with Eddie sent on to the Pacific and remembered in the village as proof that democracy can be expressed through ordinary decency.
